translations.answer: After the author explicitly defined this objective, the maintainer clarified the use of LOCAL_WORLD_ALIGNED. The thread also clarified that the fixed universe/inertial frame is fixed, while the world-aligned coincident point can move with the target frame. Since the author did not publish torque results or re-measure, this conclusion is only a reference-frame selection entry; wrench arrangement, action point, sign, and Jacobian transposition still need to be verified in the target model.
translations.applicability: Applies to the original post 'fixed world direction force, end-effector frame, mobile base robot'. Not verified for specific torque mapping implementation.
translations.credibility.rationale: No reproducible record has been formed.
translations.details.attempts.0: The author repeatedly clarified the target, and finally determined that the fixed frame force should be converted to torque.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Clearly define the coordinate axis direction and action point of the external force, then select the Jacobian reference frame.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: Distinguish between the fixed universe/inertial frame and the world-aligned expression located at the mobile body/frame origin.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: The maintainer addressed this target by using the LOCAL_WORLD_ALIGNED Jacobian.
translations.details.environments.0: Pinocchio RobotWrapper.BuildFromURDF(..., JointModelFreeFlyer()); end-effector frame; original post did not provide Pinocchio version and URDF.
translations.details.limits.0: The thread did not verify the Jacobian transposition formula, six-dimensional force/moment arrangement, signs, or action points, so this answer cannot guarantee the correctness of torque values alone.
translations.details.limits.1: No version or reproduction result is available; must verify on the target model using virtual work or finite difference methods.
translations.details.outcomes.0: Issue closed, but no author's numerical results, code, or post-verification is available.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: What Jacobian should the Pinocchio thread request to map fixed-world direction force to joint torque?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Before real-world force application, independently verify wrench order, frame transform, joint order, and torque limit.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: Misunderstood the coincident point in the WORLD convention as moving with the body.
translations.details.symptoms.0: The author mistakenly believed the WORLD frame moves with the robot, thus failing to determine which Jacobian to pair with fixed-world direction force.
translations.source.locator: Pinocchio #1761: maintainer comment 1264712803 clarifies fixed universe/coincident point; 1266647907 answers using LOCAL_WORLD_ALIGNED
